prompt: index.html is our pricing page, and it only works on a desktop screen. Make it responsive without changing its content. At 390px wide nothing may scroll sideways: the three plan cards stack in one column in their current order, and the comparison table has to fit, scrolling inside its own box if it must. Below 720px the header links collapse behind a button named "Menu" that opens and closes them, reports its state with aria-expanded, points at the links' container with aria-controls, and works from the keyboard. At 1280px keep the three cards side by side and the links visible, with no Menu button. Keep the console free of errors. Static files only; no external dependencies or assets. Verify both widths in a real browser: Playwright is already installed, import the module identified by the RUNE_BENCH_PLAYWRIGHT environment variable and use its chromium launcher. Keep screenshots inside this workspace. Do not install packages or deploy anything.
notes: A change to an existing desktop-only page, where the corpus's two frontend tasks build pages from nothing. The page has three things that overflow at 390, and the comparison table is the one a careless pass leaves behind: the wrong variant stacks the cards and builds the menu, and fails c2 on the table alone. c1 is a regression guard the untouched fixture passes. 'Collapsed' means hidden as Playwright sees it; links clipped to zero height are still shown and still focusable, and fail c3. Needs RUNE_BENCH_PLAYWRIGHT and a Chromium that can start: without one every criterion is IMPOSSIBLE, never failed. The solution and wrong trees were NOT run in a browser when this task was written (Chromium cannot start in the authoring sandbox); the sanity test runs them whenever the runtime is present.
